title: ericameria parryi subsp. howardii
intro: Ericameria parryi subsp. howardii, commonly known as Gray's rabbitbrush, is a subspecies of shrub that belongs to the sunflower family (Asteraceae) and is native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may aid in reducing pain and inflammation, as well as promoting wound healing. The therapeutic actions of Gray's rabbitbrush are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which may exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects. Further research is needed to fully understand the health benefits and therapeutic actions of Ericameria parryi subsp. howardii.
